add.issue.name: Fix lifecycle stopped-container handling, pull policy and argument validation

edit.description.md:
Source: OCR review 2026-09-09 of PRs #1-#8 (docs/reviews/), user-validated findings 1 and 3.

workspace-lifecycle.sh uses `docker compose ps -q`, which excludes stopped containers, conflating existence with running state. Validated failures: recreate on a stopped workspace reports success while keeping the same container ID; clear-caches fails because the stopped container still references the volume. Fixes: separate existing (ps -aq) vs running (inspect State.Running) queries; recreate must remove any existing container before up and assert the ID actually changed; clear-caches must remove the container reference regardless of running state.

Also: enforce the no-download contract at every up invocation with --pull never (documented compose up option; OCR suggested a nonexistent --no-pull flag); stop conflating usage errors with missing/unreadable compose files (distinct exits/messages); reject silently-ignored extra arguments for commands that take none.

edit.description.md:
Source: OCR review 2026-09-09 of PRs #1-#8 (docs/reviews/), user-validated finding 5 plus additional validated findings.

edit.description.md:
Source: OCR review 2026-09-09 of PRs #1-#8 (docs/reviews/), additional validated findings on the Dockerfile.

- Pin --platform=linux/arm64 on the base FROM so a non-ARM builder fails clearly instead of downloading the arm64 mise tarball into a foreign rootfs (validated: architecture is not enforced today).

Deferred with rationale (not this ticket): ownership robustness for pre-existing volumes/bind-mounts/user overrides — documented limitation in workspace/README.md, same class as the unwritable-state recovery already covered; ARG overridability and root-owned immutable toolchain config — folded into the provenance human decision ticket.

add.issue.name: Decide artifact provenance posture before authenticated-agent integration

edit.description.md:
Source: OCR review 2026-09-09 of PRs #1-#8 (docs/reviews/), user-flagged decisions to park for the owner.

Human decision needed before XJVWF4K (omp with real credentials) builds on the current image:

1. mise/go integrity: today the mise tarball is verified against the GitHub release-API asset digest (no standalone checksums are published; on-host byte-match recorded). Options: accept API-digest verification as-is; add SLSA attestation verification (mise publishes attestations); vendor an internal mirror with signed checksums. Trade-off: effort vs independence from the GitHub API as a trust root.
2. Dockerfile ARG overridability (MISE_VERSION/MISE_SHA256): the builder already controls the build, so this is not a security boundary today; options: keep ARGs for bump ergonomics, or freeze them as constants to make accidental drift harder.
3. Toolchain config placement: image-declared mise state lives under /home/dev (dev-writable). Options: keep native behavior (documented as not a trust boundary — same-uid code can already do anything); or move image-declared config/data to root-owned read-only paths with documented operational cost. Note MISE_PARANOID=1 currently covers fixture-tools only; extending it to base is part of this choice.

Recommendation from the review-of-review: keep the architecture; decide 1 explicitly; 2 and 3 can stay as documented choices unless the employer-laptop threat model says otherwise.

add.issue.name: Verify the mise release via SLSA attestation in the image build

edit.description.md:
Source: A5H3NY9 user decision (2026-09-09): SLSA chosen for mise artifact verification.

Replace/augment the release-API-digest-only verification in the canonical Dockerfile with SLSA attestation verification of the mise linux-arm64 tarball: obtain the provenance for the pinned release from primary sources, verify it with slsa-verifier (itself pinned by version+sha256 from its release, chain anchored and documented), checking the artifact digest, source repository (github.com/jdx/mise) and tag. Keep the existing pinned sha256 as a second lock on which exact artifact is installed. Record evidence (commands, verifier version, provenance source) in docs/evidence.md and note the remaining trust anchor honestly. add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: Implemented in PR #10 (commit a868bfa on main, rebase-merged). The mise install step in the canonical Dockerfile now runs the full SLSA chain per the A5H3NY9 decision: both digests pinned (mise tarball + cosign v3.1.3 from their GitHub release APIs), the SLSA v1 provenance fetched anonymously from GitHub attestations API keyed by the pinned digest (jq selects slsa.dev/provenance/v1), and cosign verify-blob-attestation with identity pinned to jdx/mise workflows via the GitHub Actions OIDC issuer — then the existing digest check, version assertion and root-state cleanup. Trust anchor documented honestly: GitHub APIs over TLS remain the chain root. CodeRabbit passed, no findings.

add.issue.name: Pin the validated project on every Compose invocation

edit.description.md: Full review 2026-09-09 of a868bfa, finding 1 (docs/reviews/2026-09-09-full-review-a868bfa.md). dc() invokes Compose without -p, so an ambient COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME or a Compose-loaded .env overrides the file name: the guard validates one project while stop/remove-runtime/recreate/clear-caches operate on another. Reproduced with disposable resources: with COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME pointed at a foreign project, remove-runtime exited 0 and removed the foreign container. Fix: docker compose -p $project -f $file for every invocation; add a regression proving a foreign project container and volumes survive an ambient override.

add.issue.name: Snapshot raw working-tree bytes and fail on hash errors

edit.description.md: Full review 2026-09-09 of a868bfa, finding 2. fixtures/bin/fixture-snapshot.sh enumerates with newline-delimited git ls-files (quoted/escaped non-ASCII names break the loop), masks hash-object failures inside printf, and applies Git clean/EOL filters so hashes are not the raw working-tree bytes. Reproduced: an untracked üntracked.txt with changed content compared clean (rc 0, matches) after a fatal hash error; an LF to CRLF flip under *.txt text eol=lf also compared clean. Fix: NUL-delimited enumeration with propagated failures, hash-object --no-filters, explicit symlink and missing-file handling; negative tests that content changes and EOL flips fail comparison.

add.issue.name: Revalidate durable identity before lifecycle operations reuse a saved Compose file

edit.description.md: Full review 2026-09-09 of a868bfa, finding 3. The identity record is checked only at generation; validate/start/recreate/clear-caches trust the saved file, so a state directory replaced with one recorded for another checkout is reused until regeneration. Reproduced: record canonical changed to another checkout - fresh generation rejects (rc 1) but validate and start both return 0. Fix: a non-mutating identity check (checkout from working_dir, state dir from the non-.git bind, verified via identity/workspace-id.sh against the existing record) before operations reuse state or touch containers; validate performs the same check. Regression: tampering the record after generation must fail validate and start.

add.issue.name: Propagate Docker query failures in lifecycle commands

edit.description.md: Full review 2026-09-09 of a868bfa, finding 4. is_running is used as a conditional so a failed Docker query (unreachable daemon/socket) is treated as an absent container: stop prints success and exits 0 without stopping anything, and the final echo masks the failed id substitution. Reproduced with DOCKER_HOST pointed at a nonexistent socket. Fix: distinguish query failure from empty results and propagate errors (daemon preflight, erroring existence query, capture-before-echo); regression requiring nonzero exit when the daemon is unreachable.

add.issue.name: Resolve relative HESTIA_STATE_ROOT to an absolute physical path

edit.description.md: Full review 2026-09-09 of a868bfa, finding 5. A relative state root is concatenated and used for the record and both bind endpoints: generation succeeds but start fails with invalid mount path after creating network resources, and a generated file in another directory resolves the source differently. Reproduced with a relative root and an output file in the fixture directory. Fix: resolve the state root to a physical absolute path (or reject) before deriving the state directory and writing anything; test generation and start from different generator/output directories, asserting absolute bind sources.

Implementation landed in PR #12 (commit 2fa359f on main, rebase-merged; CodeRabbit clean). Optional agent image target: omp v18.1.16 via mise, installed binary verified against the pinned release digest d8612389... and version-asserted. Durable agent state binds from <state-root>/<ws-id>/omp: sessions, agent.db, memory, logs and extracted natives persist across stop/remove-runtime/recreate, are host-visible, and clear-caches never touches them. No credentials in images/Compose/logs; missing AWS auth gives a clear actionable error (No models available. Use /login or set an API key environment variable) with shell and source fully usable. REMAINING TO CLOSE (user-owned interactive step): (1) real AWS credential login inside a workspace via the credential chain, (2) an agent-assisted fixture change, (3) session resume across recreation with a real session. Runbook: docker build --target agent -t hestia-agent:2026-09-09 . ; workspace-compose.sh --image hestia-agent:2026-09-09 --out ws.yaml <fixture-repo> ; workspace-lifecycle.sh start ws.yaml ; attach, mise trust <repo> once, provide AWS creds (scoped profile/env), omp /login or model selection as prompted; then make a change with omp, snapshot, recreate, omp -c/--resume.
